scope.comparison: clean vs deterministic color_jitter at the same restored simulator state

cls_vs_patch.conclusion: CLS and patch tokens show nearly the same divergence; the drift is not isolated to a token subset.

findings: The earliest observed residual representation is already strongly different: layer0 patch-input relative RMS is 1.28-1.43 and cosine is 0.74-0.80.
There is no later onset layer. The relative RMS difference decreases modestly with depth, while cosine continues to worsen.
By layer11 input, patch cosine is about 0.576-0.612; by layer11 output it is about 0.408-0.495.
CLS and patch tokens show nearly the same drift, so the result is not evidence for a CLS- or patch-specific correction.
No single camera is consistently most affected across episodes and frames; view ordering changes, so the failure is not attributable to one camera path.
The residual difference is distributed from the earliest image embedding through the full 12-block visual encoder.
This explains why a layer11 attention/FFN write correction or a layer11 residual-only correction is insufficient: both act after a distributed appearance-driven residual path has already formed.
The analysis is descriptive. It does not establish which individual channels or attention heads cause the drift.
limitations: Only ep10 and ep50 and fixed frames 0, 16, 32 were analyzed.
The result stores layer statistics and per-observation metrics, not full activation snapshots.
The analysis establishes distributed divergence, not the causally minimal subset of channels or heads.
next_validation: Before designing any correction, run a small fixed dose-response of the same deterministic color_jitter stress on ep10/ep50 to test whether action error and layerwise residual drift vary monotonically with intensity.
If drift and action degradation are not monotonic, do not pursue a single layer11 gate or channel intervention.
If they are monotonic, the evidence points toward input-level or multi-layer appearance robustness, not a single attention-head/FFN-channel fix.
Do not start head scans, FFN channel scans, gate training, or retraining from this evidence.
